pages.ja:
この商店街に中華飯店は一つしかない。
紅洲宴歳館、泰山。
昼なお締め切った窓ガラスは客の出入りを不明にし、一見さんはことごとく逃げ帰るという商店街の魔窟だ。
町内会からはちびっこ店長と親しまれる謎の中国人・魃さんの振るう十字鍋は、ありとあらゆる食材を唐辛子まみれにする。

pages.en:
There is only one Chinese restaurant in the shopping district.

Koushuuensaikan Taizan.

Its windows remain shuttered even at noon, concealing all evidence of customers entering or leaving. It is the shopping district’s own den of demons, from which every first-time visitor flees in terror.

The proprietor is the mysterious Chinese chef Batsu, affectionately known to the neighborhood association as the “tiny manager.” The wok in his hands smothers every conceivable ingredient in chili peppers.
pages.mirrorMoon:
There’s only one Chinese restaurant in the shopping district.
Koushuuensaikan: Taizan.
It’s an ominous dungeon in the shopping district, with no windows to show you what’s inside. Most first-time customers run away after seeing the place.
The manager, a favorite of the neighborhood association, is a strange little Chinese man nicknamed “small manager.” Batsu-san has a tendency to fill every dish with red pepper.

pages.ja:
つまり辛い。
すごく辛い。
舌を楊枝で千本刺しにされて塩ぶっかけられたぐらい辛い。
pages.jaRuby:
つまり辛い。
すごく辛い。
舌を[ruby text=ようじ char=2]楊枝で千本刺しにされて塩ぶっかけられたぐらい辛い。
pages.en:
In other words, the food is hot.

Incredibly hot.

Hot enough to feel like a thousand toothpicks stabbing your tongue before someone pours salt over it.
pages.mirrorMoon:
In other words, the food’s hot.
Really hot.
Imagine being stabbed in the tongue and then having salt rubbed into it, and you’ll be on the right track.

pages.ja:
俺が中華料理に苦手意識を持つのも、偏にこの店の味付けが地獄的だったからである。
あと、店長がこれ見よがしにアルアルを語尾につけるのもいただけない。
pages.jaRuby:
俺が中華料理に苦手意識を持つのも、偏にこの店の味付けが地獄的だったからである。
あと、店長がこれ見よがしにアルアルを語尾につけるのもいただけない。
pages.en:
The infernal seasoning in this restaurant is entirely responsible for my aversion to Chinese food.

Nor can I approve of the proprietor's ostentatious mock-Chinese sentence endings.
pages.mirrorMoon:
This restaurant’s infernal seasonings have given me a general distaste for Chinese food.
It doesn’t help that the manager keeps adding “aru” at the end of every sentence.

pages.ja:
「………………」
で、今からその魔窟に突入するワケだ。
店長に目をつけられたら高速でメニューが差し出される。
そうなったら終わりだ。
せめて注文を甘酢あんかけ系にして難を逃れなくてはならない。
pages.jaRuby:
「………………」
で、今からその魔窟に突入するワケだ。
店長に目をつけられたら高速でメニューが差し出される。
そうなったら終わりだ。
せめて注文を甘酢あんかけ系にして難を逃れなくてはならない。
pages.en:
“………………”

And now I must enter that den of demons.

The moment the proprietor notices me, a menu will appear in my hands at blinding speed.

Then it will all be over.

My only hope is to order something in sweet-and-sour sauce and escape the worst of it.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……”
And now I’m entering this terrible dungeon willingly.
The manager will bring a menu as soon as he sees me.
That’ll be the end of it.
At the very least, I’ll have to order something that uses sweet vinegar.

pages.ja: チンジャオとかホイコーローとか頼んだ日には目も当てられないし、麻婆豆腐なんてもってのほかだ。アレはやばい。舌が溶ける。地獄じゃ閻魔が舌抜くっていうが、きっとその類の地獄料理だ。店の名前も泰山だし、修行して帰ってきたっていう店長は獄卒に違いない。
pages.jaRuby: チンジャオとかホイコーローとか頼んだ日には目も当てられないし、麻婆豆腐なんてもってのほかだ。アレはやばい。舌が溶ける。地獄じゃ閻魔が舌抜くっていうが、きっとその類の地獄料理だ。店の名前も泰山だし、修行して帰ってきたっていう店長は獄卒に違いない。
pages.en: Green pepper steak or twice-cooked pork would be a catastrophe, and mapo tofu is out of the question. That stuff is lethal. It will melt my tongue. They say King Enma tears out the tongues of sinners in hell; mapo tofu must be one of the dishes served there. The restaurant is named Taizan, and the proprietor supposedly returned from some kind of ascetic training, so he must be one of hell’s wardens.
pages.mirrorMoon: It’ll turn out horrible if I order something like twice cooked pork, and mapo tofu is out of the question. That stuff is dangerous. It’ll melt my tongue. I hear the judge of hell pulls out your tongue, so such awful food could easily come from there. The manager traveled abroad to train his cooking arts, so maybe he trained with the devils.

pages.ja:
「
ふう」
時計を見ると、じき二時半になろうとしている。
学校が終わったらすぐに来い、との事だったので、これ以上躊躇している余裕はない。

pages.en:
“—Whew.”

I look at the clock. It will soon be half past two.

Tohsaka told me to come as soon as school ended. I cannot afford to hesitate any longer.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
Phew.”
It’s almost two-thirty.
I promised to be here right after school, so I can’t hesitate any longer.

pages.ja:
「
よし、行くぞっ！」
なんでたかだか飯屋に入るだけでこんな気合をいれなくちゃいけないのかって思うのだが、ともかくここはそういう店だ。
なんのつもりか知らないが、遠坂だってここを待ち合わせ場所に選んだ事を、今ライブで後悔している事だろう

pages.en:
“—All right. Here goes!”

I have no idea why entering a mere restaurant requires such determination, but that is the kind of establishment this is.

Whatever Tohsaka intended when she chose it as our meeting place, she must be regretting the decision at this very moment—
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
All right, I’m going!”
I don’t know why I have to get pumped up to go into a restaurant, but here it’s necessary.
I’m not sure what Tohsaka was thinking when she said we should meet here, but I’m sure she’s regretting it now.

pages.ja:
て。
「む？ 来たか衛宮。時間があったのでな、先に食事を進めていた」
なんか、神父がマーボー食ってる。
pages.jaRuby:
て。

なんか、神父がマーボー食ってる。
pages.en:
Or not.

“Hm? You have arrived, Emiya. I had time to spare, so I began eating without you.”

The priest is eating mapo tofu.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Wait.
“Hm? You’re finally here, Emiya? I came early, so I have already started eating.”
The priest is eating mapo tofu.

pages.ja:
「
」
言葉がない。
なんでこの場所に言峰がいるのか。
なんであんな煮立った釜みたいな麻婆豆腐を食っているのか。
それもすごい勢いで。
額に汗を滲ませて、水などいらぬ、一度手を止めれば二度とさじが動かぬわ、という修羅の如き気迫。
pages.jaRuby:

額に汗を滲ませて、水などいらぬ、一度手を止めれば二度とさじが動かぬわ、という修羅の如き気迫。
pages.en:
“——”

I am speechless.

Why is Kotomine here?

Why is he eating mapo tofu that looks like a cauldron at a rolling boil?

And why is he eating it so quickly?

Sweat beads upon his brow, yet his demonic intensity seems to declare: *I need no water. If I pause for a single moment, this spoon will never move again.*
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
”
I’m speechless.
Why is Kotomine here?
Why is he eating mapo tofu that looks like a boiling pot?
And why is he eating it so fast?
He’s sweating, but he never stops for a drink, spiritedly moving his hands as if they will never move again if he stops.

pages.ja:
というか意地になってないかあいつ、食べるスピードが尋常じゃないぞ。
もしかして美味いのか。あのラー油と唐辛子を百年間ぐらい煮込んだ地獄の釜にも匹敵しそうな料理が美味いというのか。
pages.jaRuby:
というか意地になってないかあいつ、食べるスピードが尋常じゃないぞ。
もしかして美味いのか。あのラー油と唐辛子を百年間ぐらい煮込んだ地獄の釜にも匹敵しそうな料理が美味いというのか。
pages.en:
Wait—is he simply too stubborn to stop? No normal human being eats that fast.

Could it actually be delicious? Could a dish resembling a cauldron in hell, filled with chili oil and peppers simmered for a hundred years, somehow be delicious?
pages.mirrorMoon:
Actually… Is he just being stubborn? He’s eating it way too fast.
Or is it that good? It looks as if the spicy oil and red pepper were cooked together for a hundred years just to be used in that dish.

pages.ja:
だとしたらまずい、言峰もまずいがこの店もまずい。
アレ、絶対やばげな量の芥子が入ってる。そうでなくちゃ説明できない。
pages.jaRuby:
だとしたらまずい、言峰もまずいがこの店もまずい。
アレ、絶対やばげな量の[ruby text=スパイス char=2]芥子が入ってる。そうでなくちゃ説明できない。
pages.en:
If so, we have a problem. Kotomine is a problem, and so is this restaurant.

That dish contains a criminal quantity of *spice*. Nothing else could possibly explain this.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Then this is bad. This restaurant and Kotomine are both bad.
That food has dangerous amounts of spice. It can’t be explained any other way.

pages.ja:
「どうした、立っていては話にならんだろう。座ったらどうだ」
食べながら神父は言う。
pages.jaRuby:
「どうした、立っていては話にならんだろう。座ったらどうだ」
食べながら神父は言う。
pages.en:
“What is the matter? We can hardly speak while you stand there. Why not sit?”

The priest says this without interrupting his meal.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What’s wrong? Don’t just keep standing and sit down.”
The priest talks as he keeps eating.

pages.ja:
「………………」
用心しながら……いや、もう何に用心しているのか自分でもわからないが……ともかく用心しながら対面に座る。
pages.jaRuby:
「………………」
用心しながら……いや、もう何に用心しているのか自分でもわからないが……ともかく用心しながら対面に座る。
pages.en:
“………………”

Warily—though I no longer know what I am being wary of—I take the seat across from him.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……”
I take caution as I sit across from him… Well, I’m not too sure what I’m on guard against.

pages.en:
“——”

I watch the priest closely.

…Incredible. Only two bites of mapo tofu remain.

Is he truly going to finish that…? My throat tightens. At that moment, Kotomine’s hand comes to an abrupt stop.

“——”

Our eyes meet.

Kotomine regards me with his usual oppressive stare.

“Would you like some?”

“Like hell I would!”

I answer with every ounce of strength I possess.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
”
I watch his movements.
…Amazing. He only has about two more mouthfuls left.
I watch in amazement when Kotomine suddenly stops eating.
“
”
“
”
Our eyes meet.
Kotomine watches me with his usual oppressive eyes and…
“Do you want some
?”
“I don’t want any
!”
I reply with all my might.

pages.ja:
神父はわずかに眉を寄せて、さっくりと麻婆豆腐を片付けてしまった。
……って。
もしかして言峰のヤツ、俺の返答にがっかりしたんだろうか？
pages.jaRuby:
神父はわずかに眉を寄せて、さっくりと麻婆豆腐を片付けてしまった。
……って。
もしかして言峰のヤツ、俺の返答にがっかりしたんだろうか？
pages.en:
The priest knits his brow almost imperceptibly, then promptly finishes the mapo tofu.

…Wait.

Was Kotomine actually disappointed by my answer?
pages.mirrorMoon:
The priest frowns a bit before he finishes the mapo tofu.
…Huh?
Did my reply disappoint him?

pages.ja:
……俺を待っていた人物は、間違いなく言峰神父だった。
遠坂は言峰に頼まれて、俺をここに呼ぶように言われていたらしい。
pages.jaRuby:
……俺を待っていた人物は、間違いなく言峰神父だった。
遠坂は言峰に頼まれて、俺をここに呼ぶように言われていたらしい。
pages.en:
…The person waiting for me was indeed Father Kotomine.

Apparently, he had asked Tohsaka to summon me here.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…The only one waiting for me is Kotomine.
It seems he asked Tohsaka to invite me here.

pages.ja:
「……で、一体何の用だよ。アンタが自分から出向くなんて珍しいんじゃないのか」
「なに、おまえがすでに二体のサーヴァントを倒したと聞いてな。大したものだと労いにきたのだ」
……よく言う。
仮にホントだとしたら、次は違う店に呼んでくれってんだ。
pages.jaRuby:
「……で、一体何の用だよ。アンタが自分から出向くなんて珍しいんじゃないのか」

……よく言う。
仮にホントだとしたら、次は違う店に呼んでくれってんだ。
pages.en:
“…So what do you want? It’s unusual for you to come all this way yourself, isn’t it?”

“I heard that you had already defeated two Servants. An impressive achievement. I came to offer my congratulations.”

…As if I believe that.

And if by some miracle it is true, he can invite me somewhere else next time.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…So, what do you want? Isn’t it unusual for you to come talk to someone?”
“Well, I heard that you have already defeated two Servants. I came to commend you on your achievements.”
…He’s lying.
Even if it is true, he should have picked a better restaurant.

pages.ja:
「そうかよ。悪いが、そういうのは気持ちだけで結構だ。
別にアンタのために戦ってるわけじゃない。誉められる謂れはない」
「ふむ、つまらぬ世辞は余計だったか。
では、望み通り本題に入るとしよう。凛からキャスターが生きている、という話は聞いたな？」
「……ああ。キャスターはまだ現界していて、町の人間から魔力を集めてるっていうんだろう」
「そうだ。その件と関係があるかは判らんが、おまえがキャスターを倒した夜、柳洞寺にはもう一体サーヴァントがいてな。
風貌、戦闘スタイルからいってアサシンだと思われるが、断言はできない」
「アサシン……キャスターの他にもアサシンが柳洞寺にいたっていうのか？ でもセイバーは、」

「アサシン……キャスターの他にもアサシンが柳洞寺にいたっていうのか？ でもセイバーは、」
pages.en:
“Is that so? Sorry, but the sentiment is enough.

“I’m not fighting for your sake. I have no reason to accept your praise.”

“Hm. Then I see my empty pleasantries were unnecessary.

“Let us proceed to the matter at hand, as you wish. Rin told you that Caster is alive, did she not?”

“…Yes. She said Caster still remains in this world and is gathering magical energy from the people of the city.”

“Correct. I cannot say whether the two matters are related, but on the night you defeated Caster, another Servant was present at Ryuudou Temple.

“Judging by its appearance and fighting style, I believe it was Assassin, though I cannot say so with certainty.”

“Assassin…? There was an Assassin at Ryuudou Temple as well as Caster? But Saber—”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I see. I’m sorry, but I think your words are good enough.
I’m not fighting for your sake. There’s no reason for you to praise me.”
“Hm. I guess there was no need for banal flattery.
Then let me cut to the chase. You heard from Rin that Caster is still alive, correct?”
“…Yeah. Caster still exists, and she’s collecting magical energy from the people in town, right?”
“Yes. I do not know if it is related, but there was another Servant at the Ryuudou Temple on the night you defeated Caster.
I believe it to be Assassin, judging by the appearance and combat style, but I am not certain.”
“Assassin… Then Assassin was also at the Ryuudou Temple? But Saber said…”

pages.ja: 「感知できなかったのだろう？ アサシンはそう強力な英霊ではないが、特性として気配の遮断がある。隠密はアサシンの得意分野だからな。いかなセイバーとて、アサシンが完全に引きこもってしまえば見つけようがないだろう」
pages.jaRuby: 「感知できなかったのだろう？ アサシンはそう強力な英霊ではないが、特性として気配の遮断がある。隠密はアサシンの得意分野だからな。いかなセイバーとて、アサシンが完全に引きこもってしまえば見つけようがないだろう」
pages.en: “Could not sense it? Assassin is not an especially powerful Heroic Spirit, but the class possesses the ability to conceal its presence. Stealth is its particular province. If Assassin withdrew completely from view, not even Saber would have any means of finding it.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “She did not sense him, right? Assassin is not a strong heroic spirit, but their class has the special ability to conceal its presence. Covert action is their area of expertise. Even Saber should not be able to sense Assassin if he hides his presence.”

「…………」
じゃあキャスターを倒したあの夜、柳洞寺にはアサシンがいたって事か。
キャスターを倒して安堵していた俺たちのすぐ近くで、息を潜めて俺たちを倒す機会を窺っていたと
？

「…………」

？
pages.en:
“…………”

Then Assassin was at Ryuudou Temple that night.

While we relaxed in relief after defeating Caster, it was hiding nearby, watching in silence for an opportunity to kill us—?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……”
Then that means Assassin was at the Ryuudou Temple on the night we defeated Caster.
Was he hiding near us, trying to find an opening to attack
?

pages.ja: 「……それは分かった。けど、なんだって俺にそんな事を教えるんだ。一人のマスターに肩入れはしないんじゃないのか、監督役は」
pages.jaRuby: 「……それは分かった。けど、なんだって俺にそんな事を教えるんだ。一人のマスターに肩入れはしないんじゃないのか、[ruby text=アンタ o2o=1]監督役は」
pages.en: “…I understand that. But why tell me? I thought the overseer wasn’t supposed to favor one Master over another.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…I understand. But why are you telling me all this? I thought the supervisor doesn’t help one particular Master.”

pages.ja:
「なに、これは情報交換にすぎん。私の知る事はそれだけだ。その代価として、ここ数日おまえが体験した出来事を教えろ。……今回の聖杯戦争はどうも気配が違う。
前回とは違うモノが動いている気がしてならんのだ」
pages.jaRuby:
「なに、これは情報交換にすぎん。私の知る事はそれだけだ。その代価として、ここ数日おまえが体験した出来事を教えろ。……今回の聖杯戦争はどうも気配が違う。
前回とは違うモノが動いている気がしてならんのだ」
pages.en:
“This is nothing more than an exchange of information. I have told you everything I know. In payment, you will tell me what you have experienced over the last several days. …There is something different in the air of this Holy Grail War.

“I cannot escape the feeling that something which did not exist in the previous war has begun to move.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I am merely sharing information with you. I have told you all I know. In exchange, tell me what you have experienced over the last few days. …There is something strange about this Holy Grail War.
Something is different from the last war.”

pages.ja:

“The answer is simple. My Lancer was defeated by Assassin at Ryuudou Temple. As his Master, I merely recovered the images he saw immediately before he vanished.”

The priest delivers this absurd revelation with extraordinary nonchalance.

“—What?”

“I said that I, too, was a Master. You supplied the answer yourself: one could not know without possessing a Servant.

“And you were entirely correct.”

“Y-You were——!?”

“But that was true only until yesterday. Lancer has vanished, and I am no longer a Master in this Holy Grail War. In other words, I am no longer your enemy.

“Now, have you finished with your questions? It is your turn. What have you encountered over the last several days? What have you seen?”

Well, personally, I would like either you or Rin to obtain the Holy Grail.”
“
”
…I frown.
The priest is serious.
He just said that he doesn’t need the Holy Grail.
In fact, he clearly told me that he wants either Rin or I to obtain it.

自分で叶えても、意味のない目的……？

pages.en:
“True. I possessed no wish, but I did possess a purpose. Yet it was not something the Holy Grail should fulfill. My purpose was never so earnest as that, and there would have been no meaning in fulfilling it myself.”

“…?”

A purpose with no meaning if he fulfilled it himself…?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Let’s see. I do not have a wish, but I do have a goal. My goal is not a serious matter, and it is meaningless even if I achieve it myself.”
“…?”
A goal that is meaningless if he achieves it himself…?

pages.en:
“What is that supposed to mean? Take your riddles somewhere else.”

“I intended it as the kindly counsel of an elder. You and I are alike. Neither of us possesses a definite wish, and neither of us seeks salvation.

“Therefore—I thought you might find peace if you realized the truth a little sooner.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What are you talking about? If you want to tell riddles, find somebody else.”
“Consider it a friendly warning. We are the same, you and I. As we do not have clear wishes, we cannot seek salvation.
I simply thought it would be easier for you if you quickly realized it.”

As I step outside, fighting down my heartburn, the priest calls after me.

“Emiya. I may have withdrawn from the conflict, but you and Rin remain Masters. Zouken is an insidious man. Take all the care you can.”

He offers the warning as though the matter had absolutely nothing to do with him.
